10.note: The author is speaking of the temple in Jerusalem as if it had been a **house** in which Yahweh lived. Alternate translation: [the temple]

15.note: The author is using one part of **Nebuchadnezzar**, his **hand**, to mean all of him in the act of conquering and exiling the Judeans. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when Nebuchadnezzar conquered them]

19.note: The author is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to their ancestors]

26.note: The phrase **Elkanah his son Elkanah** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended, “Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah.” This may indicate that this Elkanah was a descendent of the Elkanah named in verse 25. The purpose would be to clarify that although their names are the same, these are two different men. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [Elkanah his son, who had the same name as his grandfather]

27.note: This is the end of this verse in the standard Hebrew text as we have it today. However, some manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation add the words “Samuel his son.” This could be the original reading, since the next verse lists the sons of Samuel. You could use that reading in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [Elkanah his son, Samuel his son]

31.note: The author is speaking as if David had actually **made** the men he lists **stand over** their work. He means that David made them responsible for this work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [David made responsible for]

The author is using the term **hands** to represent activity. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the activity of leading music]

The author is speaking as if Yahweh’s sanctuary were actually a **house** in which he lived. In this context, he is describing the special tent that David set up for the Box in the part of Jerusalem where he lived, as he describes in [15:1](ta:15). Alternate translation: [in the sanctuary of Yahweh]

The author is speaking as if the **Box** of Yahweh was actually **resting**. He means that it was no longer moving about from place to place but had a permanent location in the sanctuary If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [after he moved the Box to its permanent location]

32.note: Here, **to the face of** represents “in front of.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of]

It is clear from 2 Chronicles 1:3 that the **tent of meeting** was not in Jerusalem at this time. The author explains that it was at Gibeon. So here he is using that tent to represent the special tent that David set up for the Box of Yahweh. (The author often uses elements from earlier in the Israelites’ history to represent later ones in order to depict the continuity of their worship of Yahweh down through the generations.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the special tent that David set up for the Box]

The author is speaking as if Yahweh’s sanctuary were actually a **house** in which he lived. In this context, he means the temple that Solomon built for Yahweh. Alternate translation: [a temple for Yahweh]
See how you translated the expression similar to **stood … over** in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [And they fulfilled the responsibilities of their work according to their regulations]
See how you translated the similar expressions in the previous two verses. Alternate translation: [And these were the ones with the responsibility to lead music]

33.note: The author is not referring to a specific **Kohathite**. He means the Kohathites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [From the sons of the Kohathites]

In most of this chapter, the term “sons” is literal. But here the author is using the term **sons** to mean the members of a particular group. See the discussion in the introduction to 1 Chronicles of this usage to describe members of a group who are all descendants of the figure for whom the group is named. Alternate translation: [from the clan of the Kohathites]

39.note: The author is using the term **brother** to mean that Asaph was a descendant of the same ancestor (Levi) as Heman. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And his kinsman Asaph] or [And his fellow Levite Asaph]

The author is speaking as if Asaph actually stood next to Heman, **at his right hand**, as they led music. He is using the place of honor in this culture, which was secondary to the leader in the center, to represent how Asaph was the next most important leader of music at the temple. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the next most important leader]

44.note: See how you translated the term “sons” in 6:33. Alternate translation: [from the clan of Merari]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the one standing on the left] or [the one standing at his left hand]

See how you translated the similar expression in 6:39. In this culture, the place at a leader’s immediate left was a place of honor slightly below the place at his immediate right. Alternate translation: [the third most important leader]

48.note: See how you translated the term “brother” in 6:39. Alternate translation: [And their kinsmen, the Levites] or [And their fellow Levite tribesmen]

The author is using this possessive form to indicate that this **tabernacle** was characterized by being a **house** for God. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the tabernacle that was the house of God]

As in 6:32, the author is using an element from earlier Israelite history, the **tabernacle**, to represent later worship arrangements. Since he is speaking of the time when David **appointed** these Levites, he means the special tent that David set up for the Box of Yahweh. (However, it is clear from the rest of the book that these arrangements continued after Solomon built a temple.) Alternate translation: [the tent that David set up as a sanctuary for God]

49.note: The author is speaking as if **Aaron and his sons** had actually been **offering** sacrifices at this time. He is using them to represent all of the descendants of Aaron, that is, the priests. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the priests, who were descendants of Aaron,]

The author is using **cover over** as a common expression of the culture to mean “effect forgiveness for” or “atone for.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and to atone for the Israelites] or [so that Yahweh would forgive the Israelites]

50.note: The author is using the term **sons** to mean the “descendants” of **Aaron**. In this case, he means specifically the line of eldest sons who succeeded him as high priest. Alternate translation: [were the descendants of Aaron who became high priests]

54.note: Here the term **border** represents “territory.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in their territories] or [in the territories that the Israelites assigned to them]

54.q: לִ⁠בְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ לְ⁠מִשְׁפַּחַ֣ת הַ⁠קְּהָתִ֔י כִּ֥י לָ⁠הֶ֖ם הָיָ֥ה הַ⁠גּוֹרָֽל
54.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since the first lot selected the Levites from the clan of Kohath who were descendants of Aaron]

The author is speaking as if these people were the actual **sons** of Aaron. He means that they were his descendants. The meaning of the term “sons” is the same in the rest of this chapter. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Aaron]

The author is not referring to a specific **Kohathite**. He means the members of that clan in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Kohathites]

The author means implicitly that this was the **first** lot that the leaders drew, and so they assigned cities to this group first. You could state this explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the first lot]

55.note: Here and in the rest of this chapter, the pronoun **they** in this expression refers to Joshua, the high priest Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders who assigned these cities to the Levites, as [Joshua 21:1–3](ta:21) describes. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the Israelite leaders assigned to them]

57.q: אֶת־חֶבְר֥וֹן וְ⁠אֶת־לִבְנָ֖ה וְ⁠אֶת־מִגְרָשֶׁ֑י⁠הָ וְ⁠אֶת־יַתִּ֥ר וְ⁠אֶֽת־אֶשְׁתְּמֹ֖עַ וְ⁠אֶת־מִגְרָשֶֽׁי⁠הָ
57.note: In both cases, the pronoun **its** refers to both of the preceding cities. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. It may be more natural in your language to use plural pronouns here and in verses 58 and 59. Alternate translation: [Hebron and Libnah and their pasturelands and Jattir and Eshtemoa and their pasturelands]

59.note: The ancient Greek translation adds “and Juttah and its pasturelands,” as in the parallel passage in Joshua 21:16. You may want to follow this alternative reading, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [and Ashan and its pasturelands and Juttah and its pasturelands]

The city that is called **Ashan** here is called “Ain” in the parallel in Joshua 21:16. Recall whether your translation team decided to use the same name for a given place in each instance where it appears or whether you decided to use the name that the biblical author does, even if that is a variant. Alternate translation: [and Ain]

61.note: It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [from half of the tribe of Manasseh]

The next verse makes clear that the other part of the tribe of **Manasseh** was in Bashan, east of the Jordan River, so the **half** in view here is the western part. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from the territory of Manasseh west of the Jordan River]

65.note: It is clear from the context that the author means that the Israelites gave **these cities** to the Kohathites who were priests. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And they gave to the Kohathites who were priests]

The author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. He is referring to the list of cities in verses 55–60. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which have already been mentioned by name]

66.note: As verse 70 indicates, the author means the remaining Kohathites, the ones who were not priests. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And as for the other Kohathites, who were not priests]
See how you translated the term “border” in 6:54. Alternate translation: [cities that became their territory]

71.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They gave to the descendants of Gershom]

The mention of **Bashan** makes clear that that author means the **half** of the territory of the tribe of **Manasseh** that was east of the Jordan River. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the eastern half of Manasseh]

77.note: The author means the **remaining** Levites, who were descendants of Merari. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [To the remaining Levites, who were descendants of Merari]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They gave to the remaining Levites, who were descendants of Merari]

Before this phrase, the ancient Greek translation has “Jokneam and its pasturelands, Kartah and its pasturelands,” as in the parallel passage in Joshua 21:34. You may want to follow this alternative reading, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [Jokneam and its pasturelands, Kartah and its pasturelands, Rimmono and its pasturelands]

The cities that are called **Rimmono** and **Tabor** here are called “Dimnah” and “Nahalal” in the parallel in Joshua 21:34. Recall whether your translation team decided to use the same name for a given place in each instance where it appears or whether you decided to use the name that the biblical author does, even if that is a variant. Alternate translation: [Dimnah and its pasturelands, Nahalal and its pasturelands]
